encounters.cc: Severe, intermittent right upper quadrant pain radiating to the back after eating a large meal

lines: Severe, intermittent right upper quadrant pain radiating to the back after eating a large meal

This 30-year-old female with polycystic ovary syndrome, Hurley stage II hidradenitis suppurativa, irritable bowel syndrome, and recurrent urinary tract infections, with longitudinal follow-up for IBS and HS, presents to the emergency department with a 5-hour history of severe intermittent right upper quadrant pain radiating to her back.
She reports onset after eating a large meal with associated nausea but no vomiting, and denies changes in bowel movements or urine color.
- History of recurrent urinary tract infections (≥3 episodes/year)
Her past medical history is significant for obesity.
- Dicyclomine 10 mg PO TID PRN (abdominal cramping)
- Clindamycin phosphate 1% topical gel BID (acne/HS lesions)
Smoking: Former smoker (quit 12 months ago when attempting conception).
There is marked tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant without rebound or guarding.
An ultrasound of the right upper quadrant shows multiple gallstones with no evidence of cholecystitis.

encounters.cc: Intermittent right upper quadrant pain with fever and chills for two days

lines: Intermittent right upper quadrant pain with fever and chills for two days

This 30-year-old female with obesity, polycystic ovary syndrome, and prior sphincter of Oddi dysfunction returns to the emergency department with a 2-day history of intermittent right upper quadrant (RUQ) pain that has progressively worsened.
She reports the pain radiates to her back and is associated with nausea.
She also notes a fever and chills since yesterday.
- History of recurrent urinary tract infections (≥3 episodes/year)
Her past medical history is significant for obesity and gestational diabetes, which is diet-controlled.
- Dicyclomine 10 mg PO TID PRN (abdominal cramping)
- Clindamycin phosphate 1% topical gel BID (acne/HS lesions)
Smoking: Former smoker (quit 12 months ago when attempting conception).
On examination, her temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg, pulse is 110 beats/min, and respiratory rate is 22 breaths/min.
RUQ palpation elicits significant tenderness without rebound or guarding.
An ultrasound of the gallbladder shows multiple gallstones and a thickened gallbladder wall.
There is no evidence of gallbladder perforation.
The common bile duct is dilated.

encounters.cc: Routine prenatal visit at 10 weeks gestation; no complaints

lines: Routine prenatal visit at 10 weeks gestation; no complaints
The patient with polycystic ovary syndrome and prior infertility returns for routine prenatal care at 10 weeks gestation.
She has no complaints and her pregnancy has been uneventful thus far.
- History of recurrent urinary tract infections (≥3 episodes/year)
Her past medical history is significant for recurrent urinary tract infections.
- Dicyclomine 10 mg PO TID PRN (abdominal cramping)
- Clindamycin phosphate 1% topical gel BID (acne/HS lesions)
Smoking: Former smoker (quit 12 months ago when attempting conception).
Her blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, heart rate is 72 beats per minute, and temperature is 98.6°F (37°C).
Urinalysis reveals 1+ leukocyte esterase, nitrites, and 20-29 white blood cells per high-power field.
A urine culture grows Escherichia coli with a colony count of >100,000 CFU/mL.
She is prescribed a course of amoxicillin for asymptomatic bacteriuria.
Two weeks after completing the antibiotic course, she returns for follow-up.

lines: One-week history of fatigue, anorexia, and dark urine

The patient is a 31-year-old pregnant female with a history of sphincter of Oddi dysfunction and acute cholangitis who presents to the emergency department with a 1-week history of fatigue, anorexia, and dark urine.
She reports no history of liver disease, alcohol use, or illicit drug use.
She has not traveled recently and has no known sick contacts.
- History of recurrent urinary tract infections (≥3 episodes/year)
Her prenatal screening at the first trimester was unremarkable.
- Dicyclomine 10 mg PO TID PRN (abdominal cramping)
- Clindamycin phosphate 1% topical gel BID (acne/HS lesions)
Smoking: Former smoker (quit 12 months ago when attempting conception).
On examination, she is afebrile, with scleral icterus and mild right upper quadrant tenderness.
There is no rash, and the remainder of the examination is normal.
